scope: §7.2.1–7.2.4 and §7.3.1–7.3.7; selected indirect reference behavior already tested in spec_basic_objects. Parent source/assertion review; not all parser/recovery/write sites certified.
source: Consolidated EC3 sourceMD basic lexical/object clauses; annotation index checked physical35–45: #193/#143 editorial, #365 braces only Type4, #494 octal label, #731 no comments inside hexadecimal strings, #438 equivalent escaped dictionary keys.

features.feature: Tokens, six whitespace bytes, eight general delimiters and comment line endings
assertions: lexical_spec_audit.rs literal byte sets and suffix after CR/LF/CRLF comments
features.verdict: Literal tables and token outcomes are discriminating. Type4 braces use separate function tokenizer; source footnote #365 agrees. No whole tokenizer certification.

features.feature: Object types and decimal number forms
assertions: writer no exponent/radix guard plus extreme finite roundtrip
features.verdict: Concrete source examples pass existing baseline. Writer roundtrip alone is not independent; explicit no-exponent guard adds discrimination. All range/precision paths remain residual.

features.feature: Byte strings, nesting, escapes, EOL normalization, hexadecimal whitespace and odd nibble
assertions: literal_strings_names_audit.rs Table3 and octal low-byte values, continuations, all hex whitespace
lexer.rs unescaped CR/LF/CRLF versus LFCR and <414> literal [0x41,0x40]
features.verdict: Source-derived bytes distinguish lexical semantics. Hex junk tolerance is recovery policy, not the source whitespace requirement; see D08. New limit tests pass, but they do not establish peak allocation bounds.

features.feature: Binary names and allowed writer spellings
assertions: name_escaping.rs Table4 manual pairs, escaped token followed by 12 Tf, distinct high bytes/space/slash
features.verdict: Manual pairs make this more than paired writer/parser agreement. Raw and escaped braces both legal; writer preference is policy.

features.feature: Ordered heterogeneous arrays, nested dictionaries and null entries
assertions: spec_basic_objects.rs exact mixed values/nested dictionary fields
parser.rs null entry equivalent to absent and abbreviation behavior
features.verdict: Producer uniqueness and direct-stream constraints do not impose mandatory reader rejection. First duplicate key is tolerant policy. Prior adversarial is_err tests use unclosed inputs and cannot alone prove named resource limit enforcement.

residual: Full indirect object/cross-reference semantics beyond previously reviewed controls
Peak lexer string allocation before parser size check
